recognize_zh: 這是兩張血球計數時間序列圖（非形態學影像）：左圖先天性嗜中性球低下患者 ANC 持續低於 500/µL、單核球持續偏高，沒有週期；右圖典型週期性嗜中性球低下 ANC 約每 21 天由接近 0 回升，單核球呈反向波動。
features: Serial absolute neutrophil count (ANC, blue) and absolute monocyte count (AMC, pink) plotted over about 120 days
Left (congenital neutropenia): ANC persistently below about 500/uL without periodicity
Left: AMC persistently elevated around 1000-3000/uL with a spike above 5000/uL
Right (cyclic neutropenia): ANC oscillates regularly with nadirs near zero and peaks up to about 3300/uL at roughly 21-day intervals
Right: AMC oscillates out of phase with ANC, rising during neutrophil nadirs
describe_en: This non-morphologic figure compares serial neutrophil and monocyte counts obtained two to three times weekly over approximately four months. The patient initially thought to have cyclic neutropenia shows a persistently low ANC without regular oscillation and a sustained compensatory monocytosis, a pattern of severe congenital neutropenia. In contrast, the individual with classic cyclic neutropenia shows regular ANC cycling with nadirs near zero approximately every 21 days and reciprocal monocyte oscillation. The practical point is that serial counts over at least 6 weeks are needed to document periodicity, and both disorders are commonly associated with ELANE mutations.
